quiz_item.question: Why is a sharp carving knife safer than a dull blade when whittling or relief carving, and how should you protect your holding hand?
options: A. A dull blade slices through wood grain effortlessly, whereas a sharp blade requires you to push with your full body weight.
B. A sharp blade lets you carve directly toward your bare thumb without wearing any protective gear.

C. A sharp blade makes clean, controlled cuts with light pressure, whereas a dull blade binds in the wood and slips unexpectedly under heavy force; always carve away from your body and wear a cut-resistant glove and thumb guard.
D. You should pass an open carving knife blade-first to another Scout so they can test its sharpness immediately.
choices: A. A dull blade slices through wood grain effortlessly, whereas a sharp blade requires you to push with your full body weight.
B. A sharp blade lets you carve directly toward your bare thumb without wearing any protective gear.

C. A sharp blade makes clean, controlled cuts with light pressure, whereas a dull blade binds in the wood and slips unexpectedly under heavy force; always carve away from your body and wear a cut-resistant glove and thumb guard.
D. You should pass an open carving knife blade-first to another Scout so they can test its sharpness immediately.
quiz_item.correct_answer: C. A sharp blade makes clean, controlled cuts with light pressure, whereas a dull blade binds in the wood and slips unexpectedly under heavy force; always carve away from your body and wear a cut-resistant glove and thumb guard.
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (C): Dull carving blades require excessive force and are much more likely to slip off the wood; keeping tools honed sharp, carving away from yourself, and wearing a thumb guard and cut-resistant glove prevent lacerations.

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: How is a basic triangular recess formed in a traditional chip carving design?
quiz_item.question: How is a basic triangular recess formed in a traditional chip carving design?
options: A. By drilling a center hole and scraping outward with a curved gouge
B. By making three diagonal cuts that meet at a central point to form an inside-out pyramid
C. By burning the triangle outline with a soldering iron and sanding the middle
D. By chiseling straight down along all three sides and prying the plug out with a screwdriver
choices: A. By drilling a center hole and scraping outward with a curved gouge
B. By making three diagonal cuts that meet at a central point to form an inside-out pyramid
C. By burning the triangle outline with a soldering iron and sanding the middle
D. By chiseling straight down along all three sides and prying the plug out with a screwdriver
quiz_item.correct_answer: B. By making three diagonal cuts that meet at a central point to form an inside-out pyramid
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (B): In chip carving, a triangle is formed by making three diagonal cuts angled toward a single central bottom point, releasing a three-sided chip and leaving an inverted pyramid (p. 55).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Why is a sharp carving knife safer than a dull blade when whittling or relief carving, and how should you protect your holding hand?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: Why is a sharp carving knife safer than a dull blade when whittling or relief carving, and how should you protect your holding hand?
options: A. A dull blade slices through wood grain effortlessly, whereas a sharp blade requires you to push with your full body weight.
B. A sharp blade lets you carve directly toward your bare thumb without wearing any protective gear.

C. A sharp blade makes clean, controlled cuts with light pressure, whereas a dull blade binds in the wood and slips unexpectedly under heavy force; always carve away from your body and wear a cut-resistant glove and thumb guard.
D. You should pass an open carving knife blade-first to another Scout so they can test its sharpness immediately.
choices: A. A dull blade slices through wood grain effortlessly, whereas a sharp blade requires you to push with your full body weight.
B. A sharp blade lets you carve directly toward your bare thumb without wearing any protective gear.

C. A sharp blade makes clean, controlled cuts with light pressure, whereas a dull blade binds in the wood and slips unexpectedly under heavy force; always carve away from your body and wear a cut-resistant glove and thumb guard.
D. You should pass an open carving knife blade-first to another Scout so they can test its sharpness immediately.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: C. A sharp blade makes clean, controlled cuts with light pressure, whereas a dull blade binds in the wood and slips unexpectedly under heavy force; always carve away from your body and wear a cut-resistant glove and thumb guard.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): Dull carving blades require excessive force and are much more likely to slip off the wood; keeping tools honed sharp, carving away from yourself, and wearing a thumb guard and cut-resistant glove prevent lacerations.

options: A. To soften the wood grain before making deep stop cuts
B. To make the wooden tool handles swell tightly around the tang
C. To loosen pocket lint, float away grit, and prevent rust on the steel
D. To increase friction between the blade and the carving blank
choices: A. To soften the wood grain before making deep stop cuts
B. To make the wooden tool handles swell tightly around the tang
C. To loosen pocket lint, float away grit, and prevent rust on the steel
D. To increase friction between the blade and the carving blank
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: C. To loosen pocket lint, float away grit, and prevent rust on the steel
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): Regularly checking tools, cleaning out pocket lint, applying light honing oil, and keeping the metal dry prevents rust and keeps blades operating smoothly (p. 28).
